response_queue_poisoning.description: Response queue poisoning (James Kettle 2023) — desync the response queue so the next user on the same connection gets the wrong response. The attacker sends a request that causes the server to return two responses; the second response is queued for the next user's request.

probes.description: HEAD method with Content-Length body — server sends HEAD response (no body) but includes Content-Length; proxy reads the next response as body of this one, poisoning the queue
304 Not Modified with body — some servers return a body on 304; proxy reads it as the next response

connection_state_attack.description: Connection state attack — the first request on a keep-alive connection authenticates; the second request on the same connection (from a different user sharing the pool) inherits the authenticated state because the proxy reuses the backend connection.

probes.description: Connection: keep-alive with authenticated follow-up — test if the second request on the same connection inherits auth state from the first
Transfer-Encoding: chunked with 0-length chunk + trailing request — test if the server processes the trailing data as a separate request on the same connection
